patterns.label: Attributive
patterns.explain: An attributive adjective directly describes a noun (“the old man”). It usually stands after the noun, and it agrees with the noun in gender, number and definiteness.

patterns.label: Predicate
patterns.explain: A predicate adjective makes a statement about a noun, with an implied “to be” (“the man is old”). The noun is the subject and the adjective is the predicate. It usually comes before the noun but can come after it, and it agrees with the noun in gender and number, not in definiteness.

patterns.label: Substantive
patterns.explain: A substantive adjective functions as a noun (“the old one”). It can be definite or indefinite.
